definitions.explanation: A regular or valued customer or business client, especially one with an ongoing relationship.

examples.japanese: {得意先|とくいさき}を{回|まわ}る。
{新|あたら}しい{得意先|とくいさき}を{開拓|かいたく}することが{今年|ことし}の{目標|もくひょう}だ。
examples.english: Developing new clients is this year's goal.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{得意先|とくいさき}との{信頼関係|しんらいかんけい}を{大切|たいせつ}にしている。
examples.english: We value the relationships of trust we have with our long-standing clients.

notes:
Combines {得意|とくい} (valued customer; one's forte) and {先|さき} (destination, party). A business term referring to regular customers or clients with whom a company has an established relationship. The nuance is of a valued, ongoing commercial relationship rather than a one-time buyer.

USAGE:
- Primarily used in business contexts
- Implies a B2B (business-to-business) or professional relationship more often than individual consumers
- {得意先|とくいさき}を{回|まわ}る (to make the rounds of clients) is a very common expression for sales visits

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {得意先|とくいさき}を{回|まわ}る: to visit clients
- {得意先|とくいさき}を{開拓|かいたく}する: to develop new clients
- {得意先|とくいさき}{回|まわ}り: client visits, sales rounds
- {大口|おおぐち}の{得意先|とくいさき}: major client

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {顧客|こきゃく}: customer, client — more formal; used broadly in business
- お{客|きゃく}さん: customer — general; used in shops and service contexts
- クライアント: client — loanword; common in creative and consulting industries
- {取引先|とりひきさき}: business partner, trading partner — broader; includes suppliers as well as customers
